daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo defended his frequent foreign trips, citing Indonesia's free and active foreign policy, and stated he had no choice but to attend when major leaders like Trump, Putin, and Xi Jinping invited him. He also told young entrepreneurs that he repeatedly ran for president because he believed Indonesia was heading in the wrong direction. In separate remarks, Prabowo asserted zero tolerance for corruption in the health sector.

  • A survey found that 68.8% of the public is optimistic about anti-corruption efforts under the Prabowo-Gibran administration.
  • The government's spokesperson clarified Luhut's statement on cash assistance of Rp 5.4 million per person.
  • Law and Human Rights Minister Yusril stated the government respects the verdict on TNI soldiers in the Andrie Yunus case.
  • An observer praised the National Police chief's decision to allow civil servants to occupy positions within the police force.
  • National Police chief responded to BEM SI's call for a second wave of reform.
  • An analyst suggested that the Electoral Law revision should regulate small party coalitions to reduce wasted votes.
  • The new Police Law increases Kompolnas duties and functions but provides minimal authority.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo reaffirmed Indonesia's non-aligned foreign policy stance, emphasizing the country's commitment to maintaining strategic autonomy in international relations. The Vice Foreign Minister addressed the possibility of Prabowo attending the ASEAN-Russia Summit in Kazan.

  • President Prabowo and the Canadian Prime Minister discussed new cooperation opportunities following the signing of ICA-CEPA.
  • The Indonesian ambassador said that the Indonesia-UK partnership will drive employment and economic growth.
  • Canada's ambassador stated that the eTA facility for Indonesians aims to strengthen bilateral relations.
  • Indonesia urged Asia-Pacific cooperation on future workforce skills development.
  • The National Border Management Agency invited young people to become the vanguard of border area development.

Other

The government defended the Pertamax price hike as a fiscal safeguard, with the head of Danantara explaining that market prices cannot be suppressed indefinitely. Finance Minister Purbaya said the premium fuel increase would have minimal impact on inflation, though the government and DPR are weighing stimulus measures in response. Detik reported that protesters held a late-night demonstration in Cikini rejecting the fuel price increase.

  • Bank Indonesia forecasts Indonesia's 2027 growth at the upper end of the 5.1-5.9 percent range, while the government will deploy policy synergy to boost the rupiah in the second semester.
  • Indonesia plans a national car hub with 300,000-vehicle capacity.
  • The government is pushing fee relief for small online merchants.
  • The government acknowledged that health services and handling of 2026 hajj pilgrims have not been satisfactory.
  • The Anti-Corruption Commission arrested Muara Enim Regent Edison for allegedly bribing the Supreme Audit Agency through an intermediary.
